newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money falls to 9.5/10.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money falls to 9.5/10.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money fell to 9.5/10.0 percent from 12.0/13.0 percent on Friday on ample rupiah supply, dealers said.
They said the ample market might result from moderate tax payments due on Friday because many companies would only reopen next Monday after an extended Eid al-Fitr celebration.
One dealer said the market seemed to be relaxed on the assumption of a fresh rupiah injection from Bank Indonesia after it was forced to buy some $600 million on Wednesday.
"But in fact the money policy was neutral," he said, adding that only seven billion rupiah was channeled into the market.
Dealers said tax payments might increase in the following weeks due to the approaching fiscal year-end on March 31.
But they said liquidity might not be affected next week because money withdrawn to celebrate the Eid al-Fitr was returning back to the banking system.
One- and three-month money were stable at 13.75/14.00 and 14.00/14.25 percent, respectively.

The central bank kept its rates for bilateral SBIs relatively stable. It offered three-day SBI at eight percent, seven-day at nine percent, 14-day at 10.0 percent, one- and three-month at 11.25 and 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 9.85 percent against 13.83 percent on Wednesday.
Bond dealers said prices were stable in quiet trading.
One said, however, some buying interest was seen in the PLN V bonds which triggered small increases in their prices.
The yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was steady at 15.37 percent at the price of 105.25 percent.
